title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to make first India visit on 22-23 November; $2 billion package on table
dek: Talks with Modi on Monday are expected to cover flood reconstruction aid, power trade and new air routes, including a Bagdogra link; Lipulekh remains sensitive.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah will make a State visit to India on 22 and 23 November, his first bilateral trip abroad since taking office in March, with a request for a reconstruction package of about $2 billion, new air routes and power-trade access expected to top Kathmandu's agenda, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) confirmed on Friday.

Mr Shah, widely known as Balen, will receive full State honours, call on President Droupadi Murmu and hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 23 November, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told his bi-weekly briefing in New Delhi. "This will be a State Visit and first visit to India after assuming office by the honourable Prime Minister of Nepal," he said, calling it "a very important visit for us".

## What is on the table

Mr Jaiswal said the talks would cover development cooperation, people-to-people ties, energy and connectivity, and newer areas such as start-ups, technology, innovation and sport, including cricket, which he said had become "an important connect" between the two countries. Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said the two sides expected to inaugurate completed connectivity and energy projects and lay foundation stones for new ones, according to reports. Mr Shah is also due to address a Nepal-India business forum and lay a wreath at Rajghat.

Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal are among a 34-member delegation, according to reports.

After the Bhotekoshi floods in August, Nepal is seeking about $2 billion for reconstruction of roads, bridges and other infrastructure, made up of $1 billion in soft loans, $500 million in grants and $500 million for post-flood rebuilding, according to reports. Indian officials have described a "substantive" package as being under discussion, with final terms still being negotiated, reports said.

## Air routes and the Bagdogra link

One item has a direct Bengal angle. Nepal wants more entry routes for international flights from India to its newer airports at Pokhara and Bhairahawa, which are under-used because flights must enter through the Simara route, according to reports. India has offered to open a route into Bhairahawa if Nepal lets flights to and from Bagdogra, the airport serving Siliguri and north Bengal, use Nepal's eastern airspace, reports said. A deal would shorten some routes in and out of north Bengal.

## Power, borders and recruitment

Nepal already exports about 1,200 MW of electricity to India, according to reports, and the talks are expected to cover transmission lines, access to India's power market and joint hydropower projects such as Lower Arun and Pancheshwar. The Arun-3 project is being built by the Indian public sector company Satluj Jal Vikas Nigam.

Two sensitive issues are also expected to come up. Nepal claims the Kalapani, Lipulekh and Limpiyadhura areas, which India administers, and lodged a formal protest in May after India and China agreed to resume border trade through the Lipulekh pass, which restarted on 1 August. Recruitment of Nepali Gorkhas into the Indian Army has been suspended since India moved to the Agnipath scheme in 2022, according to reports.

## Why it matters

Nepal borders five Indian states, including West Bengal, and its hydropower and rivers feed into the Ganga system that flows through Bengal. India and China have long competed for influence in Kathmandu: while Mr Shah is in Delhi, a 20-member Nepali parliamentary team is on a 10-day visit to China to discuss stalled infrastructure projects and closed border trading points, according to reports. The MEA describes the visit as part of India's "Neighbourhood First" policy.

Mr Shah, a former mayor of Kathmandu, became prime minister on 27 March after his Rastriya Swatantra Party's election victory. He visited New York in September for the UN General Assembly.

## What happens next

Mr Shah arrives in Delhi on Sunday. Agreements and any joint statement are expected after the talks with Mr Modi on Monday, 23 November.
